block.title: compile-allocated frames held a slot for every temporary
block.p: The libnanofil thread found that the λANF build of the backend overflows an 8 MB stack on one 412-block function, 13,351 frames deep in the body of merge_steps at about 600 bytes a frame. That frame was 544 bytes, but its code touched only a third of it. Regs.v laid out the plan's plain slots, and the plan gives every temporary a slot because compile mode keeps every temporary in the frame. A temporary with a register home never touches its slot, and Regs.v never uses the shadow slots of phis.

Now rplain_keys keeps a temporary's slot only when it has no register home, and a pool slot only when some key aliased to it needs one. In the λANF build of the backend, the mean frame went from 483 to 159 bytes and the largest from 84 KB to 512 bytes. The body of merge_steps takes 208 bytes. The code is the same apart from frame offsets, and it runs at the same speed on rx.ir and on the Lua, zlib and bzip2 workloads. RegsProof.v's frame theorems now take the filtered list.

claim.p: On all 53 IR fixtures, for compile, compile-promoted and compile-allocated, the arena build prints the same assembly, stderr and exit status as the OCaml build: 0 of 159 runs differ.

block.p: Smaller frames do not stop the stack from growing with the input. Two functions of the backend call themselves once for each element of a list, and neither call is a tail call. The first is existsb: on lvm.ir it holds 43,831 of the 43,841 frames at the deepest point, at 256 bytes each. Its recursive call is the second argument of orb, and CertiRocq evaluates that argument before calling orb. The OCaml extraction turns orb into (||), which makes the same call a tail call. The second is merge_steps, which conses after its recursive call in both builds.
